subject: Post-demo security discovery: log custody, erasure SLA options & next steps
messages:
From: Emma Zhang <emma@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up from demo — retention / deletion / SOC2 items

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning — the demo was really helpful. A few items our legal/security team asked me to clarify so we can move toward procurement: 

- SOC 2 status: Are you currently SOC 2 Type II certified, or is that in progress? If in progress, expected completion window?
- Log retention: we need to understand the boundary between "application logs" and "custodial logs" for PII, and how long each is retained. Our baseline ask is 90 days for audit logs but we can discuss trade-offs.
- Deletion SLA: when a data purge request is issued (via API or support ticket), what are your standard erase timelines and what does erasure look like across backups/snapshots?
- Backups & snapshots: retention period for VM/GPU snapshots and any snapshot tombstone windows before permanent removal.

I'm attaching our vendor security questionnaire to kick off. Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide (SOC 2 report, retention matrix, sample deletion confirmation)?

Proposed next step: a short call with your security lead + our security engineer to walk the questionnaire and retention options. We're targeting internal approval by mid-December.

Appended: CW-Sec-Questionnaire.xlsx (attached)

Thanks,
Emma Zhang
Senior Security Ops
ClearWell Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhang <emma@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T18:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — retention / deletion / SOC2 items

Emma — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the questionnaire. Short answers up front, then proposed options and next steps.

SOC 2 status
- Redwood: SOC 2 Type II report available for review (most recent period ends 2026-06). We can provide an encrypted copy under NDA. Laura (cc'd) can coordinate the evidence package.

Retention & custody boundaries
- Audit / access logs: default retention 30 days in hosted plans, with configurable retention to 90/365 days for enterprise customers.
- Application-level transcripts / customer data: retained per customer policy; standard hosted default is 30 days but we support pinning to longer windows for dedicated/private deployments.
- Backups & snapshots: snapshots (block-level) retained by default for 90 days; snapshot catalog entries (metadata) are tombstoned for 7 days after deletion before permanent purge to support restores.

Erase / deletion SLA (what we can offer)
- Fast Erase (enterprise add-on): permanent deletion across primary stores and object storage snapshots within 72 hours; verification report provided.
- Standard Erase (default): best-effort permanent deletion within 7 calendar days; includes deletion from primary stores and initiation of snapshot retirement; final purge follows snapshot tombstone policy (additional bounded window).
- Extended Audit Erase (for regulated customers): 30-day window to support legal hold workflows, with intermediate attestations.

Notes on backups/snapshots and evidence
- Because snapshot block retention is handled by storage-level retention, when we 'delete' an object we mark it for purge and remove logical access; physical purge follows snapshot lifecycle above.
- We can provide a retention matrix that maps data categories -> storage tier -> retention and expected erase timelines. See attached: redwood-retention-matrix-v1.pdf (attached).

Next steps (suggested)
1) Security call: Laura Bennett (Security PM) + Ben Carter (SE) to review questionnaire and retention matrix with your team.
2) We provide: NDA-protected SOC 2 Type II report, retention matrix, and a template deletion confirmation artifact.
3) You flag any must-have SLA (e.g., 72-hour erase) so we can include in the commercial terms / SOW.

Would Tuesday 12/1 or Wednesday 12/2 morning PST work for a 45-minute sync?

Thanks — happy to iterate on the matrix after the call.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-retention-matrix-v1.pdf
